note: One example is one UCF-Crime video's full UCA record: a list of [start, end] seconds and one English sentence per span (spans may overlap). UCA describes both anomalous and ordinary moments; the category comes from the file name, and UCF-Crime itself only gives video-level labels (plus frame-level ranges for the test set in a separate file). Thumbnail only, no clip (crime footage).

timeline.text: Two African-American men opened the door and entered the mobile phone store, wearing black and white vests and jeans respectively.
The man in a white vest forcibly unplugged the three mobile phones displayed on the counter on one side.
Then quickly fled the store from the gate.
Two men appeared again leaving the scene with connected mobile phones in their hands.

examples.title: Stealing080: carjacking at the roadside, 4 spans (last two share one span)

timeline.text: Two men in black ran to the white car parked on the roadside, opened the door and dragged out the people in the car
The man in white and blue who were dragged out of the car rushed to the white car and pulled out the man in gray.
Then the white car drove away.
The remaining three people ran away along the sidewalk
